overall: The AG found the Quincy Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law in its handling of the FedEx warehouse project; the mayor and developer conduct was outside OML jurisdiction. The AG reminded the Board of its complaint-response duties but ordered no remedy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board approved the FedEx distribution center project and related road work outside a properly posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that a quorum of the Board deliberated outside of a properly posted meeting and discussed either roadway improvements or construction of a FedEx distribution center, and therefore find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Mayor held a secret meeting with the real estate developer about the FedEx project.
allegations.key_passage: Individual public officials, such as the Mayor, are not public bodies and therefore, he is not subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the developer submitted falsified paperwork for the FedEx project.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review and offer no opinion on whether any actions taken by the Mayor or the real estate developer could be a violation of some other law or regulation outside the scope of the Division's review.

allegations.summary: Board did not respond to the complaint; AG raised the 14-business-day complaint-response duty on its own and reminded the Board.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board did not respond to the complaint and we remind the Board of its obligations under the Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
